name: 21862-guidedjson-1.7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1; one in-process vLLM engine.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1024, warmup the first 25% by completion, bounded at 10240 requests / 1800 s safety. 1024 is the engine's own `max-num-seqs`, so the resident decode batch sits at the admission cap -- the regime the source measured in, where `--request-rate 1000 --num-prompts 2000` kept the server saturated at a mean decode batch of ~600-840.
workload: guidellm `json_file` over `configs/prompts-json-userprofile.jsonl` -- 12288 identical rows carrying the source benchmark's own literal instruction, `"Generate an example of a brief user profile given the following schema: " + json.dumps(schema)`, which tokenizes to exactly 122 Qwen3 tokens; `output_tokens_count: 128` per row is the cap. `temperature: 0.0`, `ignore_eos: false`, `request_format: plain` (raw prompt, no chat template -- which is also how the source disabled thinking, since `--backend vllm` drives `/v1/completions`). Every request carries the ten-property user-profile JSON schema in `scenario.json` (`name` and `email` required), so a request ends when its object is complete and the realised output length sits at or below the cap.
purpose: A schema-driven profile generator returning short JSON objects from identical prompts, 1024 concurrent streams on one GPU.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
guided-decoding-backend: xgrammar
